children: By Shritama Bose and Hudson Lockett

Regulators may water down a new system that calculates end-of-day share prices after volatility spiked in the $5 trln stock market. But that would ignore the key lesson earlier adopters like Hong Kong learned: that boosting liquidity, while hard, is a more durable solution.
Full view will be published shortly.
Follow Shritama Bose on LinkedIn and X.
The Securities and Exchange Board of India on September 12 proposed a review of how settlement prices for equity index and ​stock derivatives are determined on expiry day.

The markets regulator laid out two options to tweak the newly launched Closing Auction Session in a consultation paper. The first is to blend trades from the last 30 minutes of normal trading with the 10-minute closing auction to yield the settlement price. The second entails going back ​to using only the last 30 minutes of normal trading, de-linking derivatives settlement prices from CAS altogether, at least for a year.
The proposals are open to public feedback until October 3.
